reveal_protocol: Commit-and-sample-reveal. At season close, a random sample of ~100 commitments is selected by a public randomness source outside SigningLab's control (the hash of the first Bitcoin block mined after the announced close date, applied as a seed over this sorted list). SigningLab then publishes payload and salt for the sampled entries only; anyone can recompute each SHA-256 and check the sampled verdicts against real outcomes. Because no one can predict which entries will be sampled, every commitment must be honest at publication time — falsifying even 5% of the set would be caught with ~99% probability. The full verdict set is never disclosed (it is the commercial product); payloads contain only the binary verdict and public identifiers — never model internals.
